heroHeadline: "DtMF" Extends All-Time Hot Latin Songs Record to 58 Weeks; European Tour Opens in Barcelona May 22; Webby Ceremony for "Tracking Bad Bunny" Campaign Tomorrow
heroSubtitle: Tracking the rise from SoundCloud uploads in Vega Baja to 100 billion Spotify streams, a historic Super Bowl LX halftime performance, and Grammy Album of the Year. The Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart dated May 9 confirms "DtMF" at 58 consecutive weeks at No. 1 — further extending Bad Bunny's own all-time record after breaking "Despacito" on April 29. General public tickets for the sold-out Barcelona shows (May 22–23 at Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys) confirmed on-sale and capacity on May 9, with the European leg continuing to Lisbon (May 26–27) and Madrid (June 4–5). On May 11, the 30th Annual Webby Awards ceremony in New York City will formally present the award for Best Fan Engagement to the "Tracking Bad Bunny" location-based campaign by DDB Latina Puerto Rico — the first Webby for a Latin music campaign. 'DtMF' holds 58 weeks at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs, the all-time chart record, while the Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour's European stadium run begins in 12 days.
footerNote: Data sourced from Rimas Entertainment, Billboard, Spotify Newsroom, RIAA, Latin Recording Academy, Recording Academy, Pollstar, Adidas Newsroom, The Hollywood Reporter, Variety, Bloomberg, NPR, Remezcla, Deadline, Complex, Bleacher Report, Rolling Stone, Live Nation, Estadi Olímpic Barcelona, and major media
